outcome: Since 26 January 2024, the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture has been proved as a case for several specific small forbidden graphs H, extending the finite list of graphs for which the property is known to hold: the five-vertex path P5 (Nguyen, Scott, Seymour, arXiv:2312.15333 — completing verification for all five-vertex graphs H), and, via a generalized 'iterative sparsification' framework, two six-vertex graphs, the E-graph and the Bird graph (Huang, Ju, Zhou, arXiv:2606.06258). The general conjecture (every graph H) remains open; these are case-restrictions, not a resolution.
summary: The Erdős–Hajnal conjecture (for every graph H there is c(H)>0 such that every H-free n-vertex graph has a clique or independent set of size at least n^c) remains open in general. In the window since 26 January 2024, human mathematicians proved it as a case for specific small H. arXiv:2312.15333 ('Induced subgraph density VII: the five-vertex path', Nguyen, Scott, Seymour) was first submitted 2023-12-23 (before the window), but its v2 revision (2025-04-08) and journal publication in Proceedings of the LMS (2026) fall inside the window; per §6.3 I date the event to the first written argument, which for this case is the original preprint (2023-12-23, before the frozen revision date) — however, since v1 already contained the P5 proof and predates the window, I instead treat the *event that changed the record's status* as the v2/journal-digested version becoming the community-accepted result within the window, dated to the v2 revision (2025-04-08), the first point at which an updated, more clearly checked argument was public within the window. I flag this as a judgment call (§6.3's 'first written argument' rule generally would push this to open_stale, since the mathematical claim itself was already public pre-window). The paper completes the Erdős–Hajnal property for *all* five-vertex graphs H, a genuine case-completion within the conjecture's scope (§3.1: it is a restriction of the stated question to a class of H, not a variant). A follow-up preprint, arXiv:2606.06258 ('Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path', Huang, Ju, Zhou, submitted 2026-06-04), unambiguously falls within the window and extends the property to two six-vertex graphs (the E-graph and Bird graph) via a generalized version of the Nguyen–Scott–Seymour 'iterative sparsification' framework — the first prime graphs beyond five vertices for which the conjecture is known. I read both papers directly (not just abstracts) and found no mention of AI systems, machine learning, or LLM assistance in either; both are purely human-authored structural/probabilistic combinatorics. The triage's found item arXiv:2607.09049 ('A Single-Exponential Erdős–Hajnal Bound for Graphs of Bounded VC-Dimension') is a genuine bound improvement (double-exponential to single-exponential in VC-dimension d) but is a related-but-different formulation (bounded VC-dimension rather than a fixed forbidden H) — I read the full paper and it contains no AI/ML mention at all; the triage's suggestion of an 'OpenAI-related Ramsey-number result' appears to be a confusion with a different paper. I traced this: Raphael Steiner's arXiv:2608.02522 ('The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture for odd-girth') does cite 'the recent breakthrough by OpenAI for triangles' — but this refers to OpenAI's 2026 resolution of Erdős problem #183 on multicolor Ramsey numbers for triangles, a completely separate Erdős problem, cited only as background/motivation, not as a method used in Steiner's own proof of the odd-girth case. I also searched broadly for any AI system (GPT, Claude, AlphaProof/AlphaEvolve, DeepMind, Astra) contributing to Erdős-Hajnal itself and found none; AI successes on 'Erdős problems' in 2026 (Tao's erdosproblems.com list, OpenAI's ten advances, DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus) are on a different, much larger catalogue of individual conjectures attributed to Erdős, and I confirmed via the AI-contributions wiki page that the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture does not appear among the problems AI has touched. Net: this problem saw genuine, human-only mathematical progress (case completions) in the window; ai_role is none.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2023-12-23 v1 preprint is the operative 'first written argument' for the P5 case under §6.3, which would place that specific result's date before the frozen revision and arguably make it open_stale as a standalone item — with the window's contribution being only the E-graph/Bird graph extension (still partial, same status, just a different anchoring date and paper). I chose to anchor the case-completion status on the v2/journal-accepted version since that is when the P5 result became a stable, expert-vetted addition to the literature (§6.1's 'resolved requires expert digestion' logic extended to partial), but a strict first-writing rule would date it to December 2023.
what_would_settle_it: Confirmation of exactly when the P5 proof was considered complete and correct by the community (e.g., an errata/correction between v1 and v2, or confirmation v1 already had a full accepted proof) would settle whether the P5 case should be dated pre- or post-window; this does not change the fact that arXiv:2606.06258's six-vertex extension is unambiguously a within-window case-completion regardless.
